title: Can we give a specific reason for every automated credit denial, not just cite model complexity?
description: A board-level oversight question testing whether an organization can produce an individualised explanation for an adverse credit decision on demand, rather than relying on the model's complexity as a reason not to explain.

history.note: Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources).

question_text: Can we provide a specific, accurate reason to any customer denied credit, given a reduced limit, or offered worse pricing by an automated underwriting system — and could we do so quickly enough to respond to a public allegation of bias, the way the Apple Card controversy demanded?
rationale: The Apple Card/Goldman Sachs controversy escalated publicly in part because neither side could quickly point to a specific, individualised explanation for the disputed credit-limit decision.
follow_up_actions: Request a sample adverse-action notice record and confirm reasons given are specific, not generic.
Confirm underlying contributing factors are retained and reviewable if a dispute arises.
Ask how quickly the organization could produce a specific explanation in response to a public allegation.
